result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both decks put the ask first, keep spoken lines apart from slide content and fit 15 minutes. B treats Option B more fairly: it says outright that the second shift is cheaper and faster, shows it is about 4 points short of the 30% target, and adds a slide on how the business runs for the two non-food members. B goes beyond the facts in a few places, including the 'above roughly 90%' threshold and saying Dunmore gives 'room beyond 30%' when no capacity figure exists, though it flags that gap. A's titles read more cleanly as an argument. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers state the ask on slide 1, use titles that state conclusions, define commissary and utilization in plain terms, and show that +26% falls short of the 30% needed. A is slightly stronger: its A-vs-B table makes the trade-offs clear (B is about 4 points short), and its gap list and likely questions are more thorough. B says Dunmore gives 'a second site' when it would be the third kitchen, and both decks claim Dunmore covers the 30% without a capacity figure. A also adds an unsupported 'roughly 90%' threshold.
